- Indemnity for third-party claims arising from the disclosure of our data.

I've attached our redline (HelioHealth_redline.pdf). We are prepared to move this quickly if Redwood can confirm acceptance of the carve-out and forensic access procedures.

Daniel / team —

I reviewed HelioHealth's redline and outlined Redwood's proposed compromise below. High level: we are willing to accept a targeted carve-out tied to verified misappropriation of trade secrets or willful misconduct, with narrow preservation/forensics mechanics and reasonable proof requirements. We cannot accept an open-ended, uncapped liability exposure based solely on an allegation. Proposed points: 

1) Trade secret / confidentiality carve-out: Exclude from the liability cap amounts awarded by a court or arbitral tribunal for willful misappropriation of trade secrets, or statutory remedies available to the injured party, provided that the injured party first provides Redwood with reasonable evidence of the alleged misappropriation and allows Redwood 30 days to investigate and attempt remediation.

2) Forensic preservation & access: Redwood will preserve relevant logs and runtime artifacts for a 90-day preservation window upon receipt of written notice. Redwood will provide time-limited, read-only access to preserved artifacts and will coordinate with Helio's designated forensic vendor under an NDA and a mutually agreed scope of work. Redwood will not provide administrative credentials or unmediated network access. Redwood will cover forensic costs only where Redwood's breach is determined to be the proximate cause of the loss (in which case Redwood will reimburse reasonable, documented forensic fees up to the lesser of $75,000 or actual incremental costs).

3) Indemnity: Redwood is willing to provide indemnity for third-party claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; not indemnity for claims where Helio failed to follow agreed security controls or where Helio contributed to the incident.

4) Remedies & consequential damages: Maintain existing exclusion of consequential/incidental damages, but permit recovery of direct damages and equitable relief (injunctive relief, disgorgement for willful misappropriation).

I've attached a tracked-change version with precise language (Redwood_MSA_redline_v2.docx). Please review and advise which points you can accept. If Helio insists on an uncapped indemnity for any confidentiality breach, we will need to escalate to execs for credit/insurance/underwriting approval.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Sarah / Daniel / Jordan —

Thanks for the candid feedback. After internal underwriting and a short exec review, Redwood can accept the following final compromise to resolve the deal without underwriting escalation: 

1) Carve-out scope: Damages awarded by a court or tribunal for willful misappropriation of trade secrets and statutory remedies linked to such misappropriation shall not be subject to Redwood's monetary liability cap. For other confidentiality breaches (non-willful), recoverable direct damages remain subject to the contractual cap (12 months of fees for the affected order).

2) Forensic preservation & access: Upon receipt of written notice alleging unauthorized exfiltration of Helio data, Redwood will: (a) immediately commence preservation of relevant logs and immutable snapshots; (b) within 72 hours provide Helio with read-only, time-limited access to preserved artifacts via a secure viewer or controlled export; and (c) permit Helio's vendor to perform on-site or remote analysis only under a mutually agreed SOW and NDA; Redwood will not supply administrative or privileged credentials.

3) Forensic costs & remediation: Redwood will reimburse documented, reasonable forensic fees where a post-investigation root cause analysis determines Redwood's systems were the proximate cause of the exfiltration, up to $100,000 per incident. Where Helio's systems or customer-side misconfiguration materially contributed to the incident, Helio will bear the forensic fees.

4) Indemnity: Redwood will indemnify Helio for third-party claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Redwood will not provide broad indemnity for any confidentiality incident absent a finding of Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

5) Process & evidence: Helio must provide reasonable, specific evidence (log samples, indicators of compromise, or other technical artifacts) to support a claim of misappropriation; the parties will use a short joint-triage cadence (48 hours) to determine whether immediate escalation and third-party forensics are required.

6) Implementation details: We will include the above as a specific addendum to the MSA ("Confidentiality & Forensics Addendum"). This addendum will also reference the incident classification matrix and the remediation SLA.

Attached are the final tracked redline and a short slide that outlines the forensics process for procurement. If Helio accepts, Jordan — please confirm and we'll route the final docs for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
